kubernetes: What is the smallest deployable unit that Kubernetes creates and manages?
A Pod
A container
A Node
A ReplicaSet
Kubernetes schedules Pods, which wrap one or more containers. Containers are never scheduled on their own.
Two containers run in the same Pod. How can the app container reach a sidecar listening on port 9000?
Through localhost:9000
Through the sidecar's Service name
Through the node's public IP
Through a hostPath socket only
Containers in one Pod share a network namespace, so they share an IP address and can talk over localhost.
A Pod's container keeps exiting right after start, and kubectl get pods shows a growing restart count. Which status do you usually see?
CrashLoopBackOff
ImagePullBackOff
Pending
Evicted
CrashLoopBackOff means the container starts, crashes and is restarted with an increasing back-off delay. ImagePullBackOff is about failing to pull the image.
Which object does a Deployment create directly to keep the desired number of Pods running?
A ReplicaSet
A StatefulSet
A DaemonSet
A Job
A Deployment owns ReplicaSets, and each ReplicaSet owns Pods. A rollout creates a new ReplicaSet and scales the old one down.
A new image version of Deployment web is broken. Which command returns it to the previous revision?
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web
kubectl rollback deployment/web
kubectl delete rs --latest
kubectl apply --previous
kubectl rollout undo switches the Deployment back to the prior ReplicaSet template. The other commands do not exist or do something else.
What update strategy does a Deployment use when spec.strategy is not set?
RollingUpdate
Recreate
OnDelete
RollingRestart
RollingUpdate is the default, replacing Pods gradually. Recreate kills all old Pods first; OnDelete is a StatefulSet and DaemonSet strategy, not a Deployment one.
A Deployment has replicas: 4 with maxSurge: 1 and maxUnavailable: 0. What is the most Pods that can exist during a rollout?
maxSurge: 1 allows one Pod above the desired 4, and maxUnavailable: 0 keeps all 4 available, so at most 5 Pods run at once.
Which Service type is created when you omit spec.type?
ClusterIP
NodePort
LoadBalancer
ExternalName
ClusterIP is the default and gives a virtual IP reachable only from inside the cluster.
You need a Service reachable on every node's IP at a fixed port, without a cloud load balancer. Which type fits?
NodePort
ClusterIP
ExternalName
LoadBalancer
NodePort opens the same port (by default from 30000 to 32767) on every node and forwards it to the Service. LoadBalancer builds on this with a cloud LB.
A Service has selector app: api, but the Pods are labeled app: backend. What happens?
The Service gets no endpoints, so requests fail
The Service routes to all Pods in the namespace
The API server rejects the Service at creation
kube-proxy relabels the Pods to match the selector
Services find Pods only through their label selector. With no matching labels the endpoint list is empty and traffic has nowhere to go.
What is the full in-cluster DNS name of Service api in namespace shop, with the default cluster domain?
api.shop.svc.cluster.local
shop.api.svc.cluster.local
api.svc.shop.cluster.local
api.shop.pod.cluster.local
Service DNS names follow service.namespace.svc.cluster-domain, and the default cluster domain is cluster.local.
You applied an Ingress resource, but nothing routes traffic to your Services. What is the most likely cause?
No Ingress controller is running in the cluster
The Services are of type ClusterIP
Ingress only works in the default namespace
The Pods lack a liveness probe
An Ingress is only a set of rules. A controller such as ingress-nginx must run to implement them. Ingress normally points at ClusterIP Services.
At which level does a standard Kubernetes Ingress route traffic?
HTTP host and path (Layer 7)
TCP port only (Layer 4)
Node IP address (Layer 3)
Pod labels (scheduler level)
Ingress rules match HTTP(S) hostnames and URL paths and forward to backend Services.
How are values under the data field of a Kubernetes Secret stored in its YAML by default?
Base64-encoded, which is not encryption
AES-encrypted with the cluster's root CA key
Hashed with SHA-256 so it cannot be read
Stored as plain text in the data field
Secret data is only base64-encoded. Real protection needs RBAC and encryption at rest configured on the API server.
A ConfigMap is consumed as environment variables in a running Pod. You edit the ConfigMap. What happens to the variables?
They keep the old values until the Pod restarts
They update in the container within about a minute
The Pod is restarted automatically to pick them up
The edit is rejected while running Pods use it
Environment variables are set when the container starts. Files from a mounted ConfigMap volume are refreshed, but env vars are not.
Which of these Kubernetes resources is cluster-scoped rather than namespaced?
Node
Pod
Service
ConfigMap
Nodes, PersistentVolumes and Namespaces themselves are cluster-scoped. Pods, Services and ConfigMaps live inside a namespace.
Which command lists Pods in every namespace?
kubectl get pods -A
kubectl get pods -n *
kubectl get pods --global
kubectl get pods -n default
-A is short for --all-namespaces. Without it kubectl uses the current context's namespace.
An HPA targets 60% average CPU. A Deployment runs 4 Pods averaging 90% CPU. How many replicas will the HPA request?
The HPA computes ceil(currentReplicas * currentValue / target) = ceil(4 * 90 / 60) = 6.
An HPA on CPU utilization shows the target as unknown. Besides a missing metrics-server, what is a common cause?
The containers have no CPU requests set
The Deployment has only one replica
The Pods use a ClusterIP Service
The HPA is in a different node pool
CPU utilization is measured as a percentage of the CPU request. Without requests the HPA cannot compute it.
A PersistentVolume uses reclaimPolicy: Retain. Its PVC is deleted. What happens to the volume?
It stays with its data, in the Released phase
It is deleted together with all of its data
It is wiped clean and then becomes Available
It is bound to the next matching PVC automatically
Retain keeps the PV and its data for manual cleanup. It does not become Available for a new claim until an admin handles it. Delete would remove the storage.
helm: Which file must every Helm chart contain to describe its name and version?
Chart.yaml holds the chart metadata such as apiVersion, name and version. values.yaml is optional defaults.
In a Helm chart, where do the Kubernetes manifest templates go?
Files in templates/ are rendered with values and sent to the cluster. charts/ holds dependency charts.
Charts written for Helm 3 use which apiVersion in Chart.yaml?
apiVersion v2 is the Helm 3 chart format and declares dependencies in Chart.yaml. v1 is the older Helm 2 format.
Which flag overrides a single value during install, for example the image tag?
--set takes dotted key paths. For many values, -f with a YAML file is cleaner.
You run helm install with -f prod.yaml and --set replicas=5, while prod.yaml sets replicas: 3. Which value is used?
Helm fails with a conflict error
Precedence goes from the chart's values.yaml, then -f files in order, then --set flags, which have the highest priority.
How does a template read the replicaCount key from values.yaml?
Values are exposed under the .Values object. .Chart holds Chart.yaml metadata instead.
Which built-in object gives the name chosen for the release in helm install myapp ./chart?
.Release.Name is myapp here. .Chart.Name is the chart's name from Chart.yaml, which can differ.
Which template language does Helm use for chart templates?
Helm renders charts with Go's text/template plus the Sprig function library and some Helm extras like include and required.
What does {{ .Values.port | default 8080 }} render when port is not set in any values?
The default function returns its argument when the piped value is empty or unset. Without default, the missing value would render as empty.
Why is include preferred over template when inserting a named template inside YAML?
include returns a string you can pipe to nindent
include runs faster at render time than template
template cannot accept a context argument at all
template was removed from Helm 3 templates
template writes output directly, so it cannot be piped. include returns a string, so you can fix indentation with nindent or indent.
What does the dash in {{- .Values.name }} do?
A dash after {{ trims preceding whitespace, and a dash before }} trims following whitespace.
Why are files like templates/_helpers.tpl not turned into Kubernetes objects?
Helm skips underscore files when rendering manifests
kubectl ignores every file with a .tpl extension
Helm only renders files named with .yaml.tmpl
They are excluded by .helmignore by default
Helm treats underscore-prefixed files as partials that hold named templates (define blocks) for other templates to include.
Which command renders a chart to YAML locally without installing anything?
helm template renders manifests to stdout. helm get manifest reads an already installed release.
In a CI pipeline you want one command that installs a release if missing and upgrades it if present. Which fits?
helm upgrade --install (or -i) is idempotent for both first deploys and later updates.
Release myapp is at revision 5 and broken. Which command returns it to the state of revision 3?
helm rollback takes the release name and a revision number. helm history myapp lists the available revisions.
By default, where does Helm 3 store release records?
In Secrets in the release's namespace
In ConfigMaps in the kube-system namespace
In the ~/.helm folder on the client
Helm 3 removed Tiller and stores each revision as a Secret in the release namespace. Helm 2 used ConfigMaps in kube-system.
In a Helm 3 chart (apiVersion v2), where are chart dependencies declared?
In the dependencies list of Chart.yaml
In requirements.yaml at the chart root
In values.yaml under a deps key
Helm 3 charts list dependencies in Chart.yaml. requirements.yaml was the Helm 2 location. helm dependency update downloads them into charts/.
Your chart depends on a subchart named redis. How do you set the subchart's auth.enabled from the parent's values.yaml?
Values under a top-level key that matches the subchart name are passed to that subchart. global values are shared with all subcharts.
Which annotation makes a Job run as a Helm hook before an upgrade, for example to run database migrations?
Hook types include pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade and post-upgrade. hook-weight only orders hooks of the same type.
A hook Job fails on the second upgrade because a Job with that name already exists. Which setting fixes this?
before-hook-creation deletes the previous hook resource before creating the new one. resource-policy: keep does the opposite and preserves resources.
terraform: In HCL, which block type declares an infrastructure object that Terraform creates and manages?
resource
data
provider
locals
resource blocks describe managed objects. data blocks only read existing information, and provider blocks configure the plugin.
How do you reference the id attribute of resource "aws_instance" "web" elsewhere in the configuration?
aws_instance.web.id
resource.aws_instance.web.id
${aws_instance}.web.id
var.aws_instance.web.id
References use TYPE.NAME.ATTRIBUTE. Such references also create an implicit dependency between resources.
Which command must you run first in a fresh Terraform working directory, to download providers and set up the backend?
terraform init
terraform plan
terraform get
terraform validate
terraform init installs providers and modules and configures the backend. plan and apply fail until init has run.
A provider has version = "~> 5.0". Which versions are allowed?
Exactly 5.0.0
Any version >= 5.0
The pessimistic operator allows only the rightmost given component to grow. With ~> 5.0 that is the minor version, so 6.0 is excluded.
You need to look up an existing VPC that Terraform does not manage, to use its ID. Which block fits?
A data block
A moved block
A locals block
An output block
Data sources read existing infrastructure without managing its lifecycle.
A resource uses count over a list of three names. You delete the first name. What does the plan typically show?
Remaining items change because their indexes shift
Only the first instance is destroyed, nothing else
No changes appear until you run terraform refresh
An error, because count lists cannot shrink
count tracks instances by index, so removing an early element shifts the others. for_each with a set or map keys instances by name and avoids this.
What is the default name of the local state file Terraform writes?
terraform.tfstate
main.tfstate
.terraform/state.json
terraform.tfvars
Without a remote backend, state is written to terraform.tfstate in the working directory. terraform.tfvars holds variable values.
Why do teams move Terraform state to a remote backend such as S3 or Terraform Cloud?
Shared state with locking against concurrent runs
Remote state makes plan and apply run faster
Remote backends strip secrets out of the state
Providers only work when state is stored remotely
Remote backends give everyone the same state and, when supported, lock it during operations. State can still contain secrets, so access must be restricted.
An apply crashed and left the state locked. After confirming no one else is running Terraform, which command clears the lock?
terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID
terraform state rm lock
terraform init -reconfigure
terraform refresh -unlock
force-unlock removes a stuck lock by its ID. Use it only when you are sure no other operation is in progress.
A database was created by hand and you now wrote a matching resource block. How do you bring it under Terraform management without recreating it?
Import it into state (CLI or import block)
Run terraform apply with -refresh-only
Run terraform taint on the resource
Copy its ID into the terraform.tfvars file
Import links the existing object to the resource address in state. Afterwards plan should show no changes if the config matches.
You rename resource aws_s3_bucket.logs to aws_s3_bucket.audit_logs in the code. How do you avoid destroying and recreating the bucket?
Add a moved block or run terraform state mv
Run terraform apply -replace on the old name
Change the bucket's tags to the new name
Delete terraform.tfstate and re-import all
moved blocks (Terraform 1.1 and later) or terraform state mv change the address in state, so Terraform sees a rename instead of a new resource.
Variable region has a default of us-east-1, terraform.tfvars sets eu-west-1, and you run terraform apply -var="region=ap-south-1". Which value is used?
ap-south-1
eu-west-1
us-east-1
An error is raised
Command-line -var and -var-file options have the highest precedence, above tfvars files, TF_VAR_ environment variables and defaults.
Both TF_VAR_region in the environment and region in terraform.tfvars are set, with no -var flag. Which wins?
The value in terraform.tfvars
The TF_VAR_region environment value
The variable's default
Whichever was changed most recently
Environment variables have lower precedence than terraform.tfvars, which is loaded automatically.
An output is marked sensitive = true. What does that change?
Hidden in CLI output, but still in state
It is encrypted inside the state file
It is removed from the state file entirely
It can no longer be used by other modules
sensitive only redacts the value in plan and apply output. The plain value is still in state, which must be protected.
A module call is named network and the module defines output vpc_id. How does the root module read it?
module.network.vpc_id
output.network.vpc_id
network.outputs.vpc_id
var.network.vpc_id
Child module outputs are exposed as module.NAME.OUTPUT. Only declared outputs are visible to the caller.
You add a new module block with source = "./modules/vpc" and run terraform plan. It errors that the module is not installed. What fixes it?
Run terraform init again
Run terraform get -update=false
Add the module to required_providers
Run terraform fmt -recursive
terraform init installs modules referenced by the configuration, including local ones, whenever module blocks are added or their sources change.
Which workflow guarantees that apply executes exactly the changes you reviewed?
terraform plan -out=tfplan, then terraform apply tfplan
terraform plan, then terraform apply -auto-approve
terraform apply -refresh=false after a fresh plan
terraform validate -json, then terraform apply -auto-approve
A saved plan file is applied as-is without a new plan. A plain apply recalculates and could differ if anything changed meanwhile.
In terraform plan output, what does the -/+ symbol next to a resource mean?
It will be destroyed and then recreated
It will be updated in place
It will be read as a data source
It will be removed from state only
-/+ means replacement, often because an argument that forces a new resource changed. ~ means update in place.
Replacing a resource causes downtime because Terraform deletes the old one first. Which setting makes it create the new one first?
lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }
lifecycle { replace_triggered_by = [self] }
lifecycle { ignore_changes = all }
create_before_destroy reverses the order for replacements. prevent_destroy blocks destruction entirely and makes the plan fail.
In Terraform 1.x, which command forces a single healthy resource to be recreated on the next apply?
terraform apply -replace="aws_instance.web"
terraform apply -recreate=aws_instance.web
terraform state rm aws_instance.web
terraform refresh -target=aws_instance.web
-replace (available since 0.15.2) is the recommended replacement for terraform taint. state rm only forgets the resource and leaves it running.
ansible: In which format are Ansible playbooks written?
Playbooks are YAML documents containing a list of plays.
Inside a play, which key selects the machines the tasks run on?
hosts takes a pattern such as a group name, a host name or all, matched against the inventory.
Your tasks install packages and need root. What do you add to the play?
become enables privilege escalation, which uses sudo by default. become_user changes the target user.
What does ansible all -m ping actually test?
SSH login and a usable Python on each host
Open port 22 only, without logging in
The ping module is not ICMP. It logs in, runs a small module and returns pong, proving connectivity and Python work.
A task must run grep ERROR /var/log/app.log | wc -l. Which module supports the pipe?
command does not go through a shell, so pipes, redirects and variables like $HOME do not work. shell runs the line through /bin/sh.
You want a config file where Jinja2 variables are filled in per host. Which module fits?
template renders a .j2 file with Jinja2 on the controller and copies the result. copy transfers files as they are.
Which module installs nginx on an Ubuntu host in an idempotent way?
The apt module checks whether the package is already installed and reports ok instead of changed. Raw commands run every time.
In an INI inventory, which line defines a group named web?
INI inventories use [groupname] headers followed by host lines. In YAML inventories, groups sit under the children key of all.
Which built-in group contains every host in the inventory?
all always includes all hosts. ungrouped holds hosts that belong to no other group.
A host is listed as db1 but its real IP is 10.0.0.5. Which inventory variable tells Ansible where to connect?
ansible_host sets the actual address to connect to, while db1 remains the inventory name. ansible_user sets the SSH user.
Where do you put variables that should apply to every host in group web?
Files in group_vars named after a group are loaded for its hosts. host_vars files are named after individual hosts.
Which file does Ansible run as the main task list of a role named nginx?
Each role directory such as tasks, handlers or defaults uses main.yml as its entry point.
A role should let users easily override its port. Where should the default value go?
Role defaults have the lowest variable precedence, so inventory or play vars override them. Role vars rank much higher and are hard to override.
When does a notified handler run by default?
Once, after all tasks in the play finish
Once per task that notifies it
Only on the next playbook run
Handlers are queued and run once at the end of the play, no matter how many tasks notified them.
A template task has notify: restart nginx, but the rendered file is identical to the one on the server. What happens?
The handler does not run because the task reported ok
The handler runs because notify is always triggered
The handler runs only in check mode
Ansible fails because the file did not change
Handlers run only when the notifying task reports changed. This keeps restarts to cases where something actually changed.
You need a notified handler to run in the middle of a play, before later tasks. What do you add?
meta: flush_handlers runs all pending handlers at that point. force_handlers makes handlers run even when a later task fails.
What does {{ port | default(80) }} render in a Jinja2 template when port is undefined?
The default filter supplies a fallback for undefined variables.
Why must you quote a YAML value that starts with a Jinja2 expression, as in msg: "{{ greeting }} world"?
YAML would read an unquoted { as a mapping
Jinja2 ignores expressions that are unquoted
Quotes mark the value as a vaulted secret
Ansible needs quotes to turn templating on
A value beginning with { looks like an inline YAML dictionary, so the parser fails. Quoting the whole value avoids that.
You run the same playbook twice on a host with no outside changes. In a well-written playbook, what should the second run report?
changed equal to the task count
Idempotent tasks check current state and change only what differs, so a second run finds nothing to do.
A command task runs an installer that should run only once. Which argument keeps it idempotent?
once: true on the command task
idempotent: yes on the command task
run_once: true on the command task
With creates, the command is skipped if the given path exists. changed_when only changes how the result is reported.
nginx: Which directive inside a location block forwards requests to an app on 127.0.0.1:3000?
proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
upstream http://127.0.0.1:3000;
proxy_pass sends the request to the given address or upstream group. upstream is a separate block that defines a group of servers.
Config: location /api/ { proxy_pass http://app:8080/; }. A client requests /api/users. Which path does the backend receive?
/users
/api/users
/api//users
/8080/api/users
When proxy_pass includes a URI (here the trailing slash), the matched location prefix /api/ is replaced by it. Without a URI the full /api/users is passed.
Behind Nginx, your app sees every request's Host as the upstream name instead of the public domain. Which line fixes it?
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_pass_header Host;
add_header Host $host;
proxy_redirect Host $host;
By default Nginx sends the proxy_pass host as Host. proxy_set_header Host $host passes the client's original host. add_header only affects responses.
Which line passes the client IP chain to the backend in the standard header?
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $server_addr:$server_port;
add_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr always;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $host$request_uri;
$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for appends $remote_addr to any incoming X-Forwarded-For value.
WebSocket connections through your Nginx proxy fail. Which settings are needed besides proxy_pass?
HTTP/1.1 plus Upgrade and Connection headers
proxy_buffering off plus gzip compression on
keepalive_timeout 0 plus HTTP/2 on the listener
ssl_protocols TLSv1.3 plus http2 on the server
WebSockets need an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade handshake. Nginx must forward the Upgrade and Connection headers explicitly because they are hop-by-hop.
Which load balancing method does an upstream block use when you specify none?
Round robin
Least connections
IP hash
Random choice
Nginx defaults to weighted round robin. least_conn, ip_hash, hash and random must be set explicitly.
Requests have very uneven processing times, and some backends pile up slow requests. Which upstream directive helps most?
least_conn;
ip_hash;
keepalive 32;
zone backend 64k;
least_conn sends each request to the server with the fewest active connections, which suits uneven request durations.
An app stores sessions in memory, so a user must keep hitting the same backend. Which built-in upstream method fits without extra modules?
ip_hash;
least_conn;
round_robin;
random;
ip_hash maps a client IP to the same server. round_robin is not a directive; round robin is simply the default.
Upstream: server a weight=3; server b;. Out of 8 requests under the default method, about how many go to a?
Weights 3 and 1 give a three-to-one split, so a gets 6 of 8 requests and b gets 2.
Which pair of directives does a server block need to serve HTTPS with your certificate?
ssl_certificate and ssl_certificate_key
ssl_cert_file and ssl_key_file
tls_certificate and tls_private_key
ssl_trusted_certificate and ssl_dhparam
With listen 443 ssl, ssl_certificate points to the certificate (chain) and ssl_certificate_key to its private key.
Some mobile clients reject your site's certificate, while desktop browsers accept it. What is a common Nginx-side cause?
The certificate file lacks the intermediates
ssl_session_cache is turned off in the server
The server block does not enable http2
The private key file has 0600 permissions
ssl_certificate should contain the server certificate followed by intermediates (the full chain). Desktop browsers may fill gaps; many clients do not.
Which line in a port 80 server block redirects all traffic to HTTPS while keeping the host and path?
return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
rewrite ^ https://$host permanent;
return 301 https://$server_addr$uri;
proxy_pass https://$host$request_uri;
return 301 with $host and $request_uri keeps the requested domain, path and query string. The rewrite shown drops the path.
A request's Host header matches no server_name. Which server block handles it?
The default_server for that port, or the first
The server block with the longest server_name
None; Nginx returns 404 immediately
The block whose root contains an index.html
Nginx falls back to the server marked default_server on the listen directive, or the first server block for that address and port.
Config has location /images/ { } and location ~* \.(png|jpg)$ { }. Which block handles /images/cat.png?
The regex location
The /images/ prefix location
Both, merged in order
Neither; Nginx returns 404
Nginx remembers the longest prefix match, then checks regex locations in order and uses the first that matches. Adding ^~ to the prefix would stop the regex check.
What does location = / { } match?
Only the exact URI /
Every URI that starts with /
Only URIs ending in a slash
The root directory and its files
The = modifier is an exact match and is checked first, so it is a fast way to handle the home page.
A React single-page app served by Nginx returns 404 when you refresh /dashboard. Which directive fixes it?
try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
index index.html index.htm;
error_page 404 /404.html;
autoindex on; in the location
try_files serves the file if it exists, and otherwise falls back to index.html so the client-side router handles the path.
Config: location /static/ { root /var/www; }. Which file is served for /static/app.css?
/var/www/static/app.css
/var/www/app.css
/static/var/www/app.css
/var/www/html/static/app.css
root appends the full URI to the path. alias /var/www/; would replace the /static/ prefix and serve /var/www/app.css.
You set up proxy_cache_path and proxy_cache. How can you see whether a response was served from cache?
Add a header with $upstream_cache_status
Check $request_time in the response
Read the X-Cache header Nginx adds by default
Enable proxy_buffering and check the logs
add_header X-Cache-Status $upstream_cache_status; exposes values like HIT, MISS or EXPIRED. Nginx does not add such a header by itself.
Config: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s; then limit_req zone=api burst=20;. What happens to a burst of 25 requests at once from one IP?
About 20 wait in a queue and the rest get rejected
All 25 are served at the same moment
All 25 are rejected as a single burst
10 are served and the other 15 wait in a queue
burst allows up to 20 excess requests to queue and be released at 10 per second. Requests beyond the burst are rejected. nodelay would serve queued ones immediately.
When limit_req rejects a request and limit_req_status is not set, which status code does Nginx return?
The default is 503 Service Unavailable. Many setups use limit_req_status 429; to return Too Many Requests instead.
aws: A user has an IAM policy that allows s3:DeleteObject and another that explicitly denies it. What is the result?
Denied, because an explicit deny overrides any allow
Allowed, because allow statements are evaluated first
Allowed only if the bucket policy agrees
It depends on which policy was attached last
In IAM evaluation, an explicit Deny in any applicable policy always wins over Allow statements.
A new IAM role has no policies attached. What can it do?
Nothing; everything is implicitly denied
Read-only access to all AWS services
Full access within its own account
Only actions inside the IAM service
AWS denies by default. Permissions exist only where a policy explicitly allows them.
An app on EC2 needs to read from S3. What is the recommended way to give it credentials?
Attach an IAM role through an instance profile
Store an access key in the app's config file
Put the root user's keys in env variables
Make the bucket public for the instance
An instance role provides temporary, auto-rotated credentials through the metadata service, so no long-lived keys sit on the server.
What does the trust policy of an IAM role control?
Which principals may assume the role
Which actions the role may perform
Which regions the role is valid in
How long the role's password lasts
The trust policy lists who can call sts:AssumeRole. Permission policies attached to the role decide what it can do.
Security group rule allows inbound TCP 443. Do you need an outbound rule for the responses?
No, security groups are stateful
Yes, ephemeral ports must be opened
Yes, unless the VPC has a NAT gateway
No, because outbound is always blocked
Security groups track connections, so return traffic is allowed automatically. Network ACLs are stateless and need rules in both directions.
You need to block one specific IP address from reaching a subnet. Which feature supports an explicit deny rule?
A network ACL
A security group
An IAM policy
A route table
Security groups support only allow rules. Network ACLs support both allow and deny and apply at the subnet level.
An EC2 instance is stopped and started again. What happens to data on an instance store volume?
It is lost, as the storage is temporary
It is kept, just like on an EBS volume
It is moved to an EBS snapshot first
It is kept only if termination protection is on
Instance store is physically attached temporary storage and does not survive stop or termination. EBS volumes persist independently.
By default, when does an EC2 user data shell script run?
Once, at the first boot of the instance
At every boot, including after a reboot
Every time a user connects with SSH
Only when the instance is stopped
cloud-init runs user data scripts on first launch by default. Running it every boot needs extra configuration.
A bucket policy grants public s3:GetObject with Resource "arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket", but downloads still fail. What is wrong in the policy?
The resource needs the /* object suffix
The action must be s3:ListBucket instead
The principal must be the root user
The effect must be AllowPublic instead
Object actions apply to object ARNs, which need the /* suffix. The bare bucket ARN covers bucket-level actions like ListBucket.
A bucket policy allows public read, yet anonymous requests get 403. Which setting most likely overrides the policy?
S3 Block Public Access
Bucket versioning enabled
Default encryption with SSE-S3
Transfer Acceleration
Block Public Access settings at the bucket or account level override policies and ACLs that grant public access.
What makes a VPC subnet public?
A default route to an internet gateway
A tag with the word public in its name
A NAT gateway placed inside the subnet
A CIDR block of exactly /24 in size
A public subnet is defined by routing: a default route to an internet gateway. Instances also need a public IP to be reachable.
Instances in a private subnet must download updates from the internet but stay unreachable from it. What do you add?
A NAT gateway in a public subnet, plus a route to it
An internet gateway attached directly to the private subnet
A security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 inbound
VPC peering with the account's default VPC
A NAT gateway allows outbound connections initiated from private instances while blocking unsolicited inbound traffic.
How many IP addresses can you assign to resources in a /24 subnet in an AWS VPC?
A /24 has 256 addresses and AWS reserves 5 in every subnet (network, router, DNS, future use and broadcast), leaving 251.
What is the maximum configurable timeout of a single AWS Lambda invocation?
15 minutes
5 minutes
1 hour
30 seconds
Lambda functions can run up to 900 seconds. Longer jobs fit better in ECS, Batch or Step Functions.
A Lambda function gets AccessDenied when writing to DynamoDB. Where should you add the permission?
To the function's execution role
To the function's environment variables
To the caller's resource policy only
To the DynamoDB table's security group
Lambda code runs with the credentials of its execution role, so that role needs dynamodb:PutItem on the table.
A Lambda handler caches a database connection in a global variable. What happens on later invocations?
Warm invocations in the same environment reuse it
It is rebuilt from scratch on every single invocation
The function fails, as globals are forbidden in Lambda
All instances share it across machines
Code outside the handler runs once per execution environment and is reused while that environment stays warm. It is not shared between environments.
In Amazon ECS, which role does the agent use to pull images from ECR and send logs to CloudWatch?
The task execution role
The task role (taskRoleArn)
The service-linked role for EC2
The container instance's SSH key
The execution role is used by ECS itself to pull images and write logs. The task role is the identity your application code uses.
A team wants to run containers without managing any EC2 servers. Which launch option fits ECS or EKS?
Running on AWS Fargate
EC2 Auto Scaling groups
Elastic Beanstalk worker tier
EC2 Dedicated Hosts
Fargate is serverless compute for containers: you define CPU and memory per task or Pod and AWS manages the hosts.
What is the main purpose of enabling Multi-AZ on an Amazon RDS instance?
Automatic failover to a standby in another AZ
Spreading read queries across replicas
Lower cost through shared storage
Running two engines on one instance
Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby for high availability. In the classic setup the standby serves no reads; read replicas handle read scaling.
You want a CloudWatch alarm on an EC2 instance's memory usage, but no memory metric exists. Why?
Memory needs the CloudWatch agent on the instance
Memory metrics require a Dedicated Host
Memory is shown only under ECS metrics
Detailed monitoring must be disabled first
EC2 reports hypervisor-visible metrics like CPU and network. Memory and disk usage come from inside the OS, so the CloudWatch agent must publish them.
gcp: In Google Cloud, what is a service account?
An identity used by workloads and apps, not people
A billing account that is shared by a whole team
A Google Workspace user account with admin rights
A project-level bucket that tracks API quota
Service accounts let VMs, functions and other code authenticate to Google APIs and receive IAM roles.
You grant a role on a project. Which resources does the grant apply to?
All resources in the project, via inheritance
Only resources created after the grant itself
Only the billing settings of the project
Only resources located in the default region
IAM policies are inherited down the hierarchy: organization, folders, projects, then resources. A project grant covers everything below it.
Why does Google recommend predefined roles such as roles/storage.objectViewer over the basic Editor role?
Basic roles grant broad access across many services
Basic roles cannot be granted to service accounts at all
Predefined roles are billed less for each API request
Editor is limited to resources in a single region
Owner, Editor and Viewer span almost all services. Predefined and custom roles follow least privilege.
A GitHub Actions pipeline must deploy to GCP. What is the recommended way to authenticate without storing long-lived keys?
Workload Identity Federation
A service account JSON key in a repo secret
A personal user's OAuth refresh token
An API key with project-wide scope
Workload Identity Federation exchanges the CI provider's OIDC token for short-lived Google credentials, so no key file needs to be stored.
Code on a Compute Engine VM calls Google APIs with the client library and no key file. Which identity does it use?
The service account attached to the VM
The user account that created the VM
The project owner's personal account
An anonymous unauthenticated identity
Client libraries use Application Default Credentials, which on a VM come from the metadata server for the attached service account.
A batch job is fault-tolerant and should run as cheaply as possible on Compute Engine. Which VM option fits?
Spot VMs
Sole-tenant nodes
Reserved VMs
Shielded VMs
Spot (and older preemptible) VMs are heavily discounted but can be stopped by Google at any time, which suits restartable batch work.
A managed instance group creates identical VMs and autoscales them. What does it use as the blueprint for new VMs?
An instance template
A machine image of the first VM
A snapshot schedule
A Deployment Manager config
Managed instance groups create VMs from an instance template that defines machine type, image, disks and metadata.
Which metadata key runs a script on a Linux Compute Engine VM each time it boots?
startup-script
user-data
boot-command
init-script
The startup-script metadata key (or startup-script-url) runs on every boot. user-data is the AWS EC2 naming.
You created a GKE cluster. Which command configures kubectl to talk to it?
gcloud container clusters get-credentials NAME
gcloud container clusters connect NAME --kubeconfig
kubectl config import NAME --provider gcp
gcloud compute ssh NAME --kubeconfig ~/.kube
get-credentials writes the cluster endpoint and auth settings into your kubeconfig.
What is the key difference between GKE Autopilot and GKE Standard?
In Autopilot, Google manages the nodes for you
Autopilot has no Kubernetes API access
Standard clusters cannot use autoscaling
Autopilot runs only on Spot VMs
Autopilot manages node provisioning and scaling and bills by Pod resource requests. In Standard you manage node pools yourself.
Pods in GKE need to call Cloud Storage as a specific IAM identity, without key files. Which feature fits?
Workload Identity Federation for GKE
Node access scopes set to full cloud-platform
A Kubernetes Secret holding a JSON key file
Binary Authorization for the workloads
Workload Identity maps Kubernetes service accounts to IAM, so each workload gets its own short-lived credentials instead of sharing the node's identity.
You must keep backup files rarely accessed, about once a year, at the lowest storage cost. Which Cloud Storage class fits?
Archive
Standard
Nearline
Regional SSD
Archive is designed for data accessed less than once a year (with a 365-day minimum storage duration). Nearline targets roughly monthly access.
What does enabling uniform bucket-level access on a Cloud Storage bucket do?
Disables object ACLs so only IAM controls access
Makes all objects in the bucket publicly readable
Replicates the bucket to every region automatically
Encrypts objects with a customer-managed key
With uniform access, per-object ACLs are turned off and permissions come only from bucket-level IAM policies.
A user without a Google account must download one private object for the next hour. Which feature fits?
A signed URL with a one-hour expiry
Making the bucket public for an hour
Adding allUsers as Viewer to the project
A Cloud CDN cache key for the object
Signed URLs grant time-limited access to a specific object to anyone who has the link.
Logs in a bucket should move to Coldline after 30 days and be deleted after 365 days. What do you configure?
Object Lifecycle Management rules
A Cloud Scheduler job per object
Retention policy with bucket lock
Object versioning on the bucket
Lifecycle rules apply actions such as SetStorageClass and Delete based on conditions like object age.
A Cloud Function should run whenever a file is uploaded to a bucket. What kind of trigger is this?
An event-driven trigger on Cloud Storage
An HTTP trigger called by the bucket
A Cloud Scheduler cron trigger
A Pub/Sub pull subscription you poll
Cloud Functions support HTTP triggers and event triggers. A Cloud Storage object finalize event fires the function on upload.
Cloud Functions 2nd gen (now Cloud Run functions) is built on which Google Cloud products?
Cloud Run and Eventarc
App Engine and Pub/Sub
GKE Autopilot and Cloud Tasks
Compute Engine and Cloud Build
2nd gen functions run on Cloud Run infrastructure and use Eventarc for event delivery, which enables features like concurrency per instance.
In BigQuery with on-demand pricing, does adding LIMIT 10 to SELECT * FROM a large unclustered table reduce the bytes billed?
No, the chosen columns are still fully scanned
Yes, only the first 10 rows are read and billed
Yes, the billing drops by about 90 percent
No, because SELECT * queries are free of charge
On-demand billing depends on bytes scanned in the referenced columns. LIMIT does not reduce the scan; selecting fewer columns or partition filters do.
How do Google Cloud VPC networks and subnets relate to regions?
The VPC is global, and each subnet is regional
The VPC is regional, and each of its subnets is zonal
Both the VPC and its subnets are zonal
Both the VPC and its subnets are global
A single GCP VPC can span all regions, with subnets defined per region. This differs from AWS, where a VPC is regional.
VMs without external IP addresses must reach Cloud Storage APIs. Which subnet setting enables this?
Private Google Access
Cloud Armor policy
Auto mode subnet creation
VPC Network Peering
Private Google Access lets internal-only VMs reach Google APIs. Cloud NAT is for reaching the general internet.
azure: You delete an Azure resource group that contains a VM, a disk and a storage account. What happens to those resources?
They are all deleted with the group
They move to the default resource group
They stay but become unmanaged
Only the VM is deleted, the rest stay
A resource group is a lifecycle container, so deleting it deletes everything inside. Resource locks can prevent accidental deletion.
A resource group is created in West Europe. Can a VM inside it live in East US?
Yes, the group's location only stores its metadata
No, all resources must share the group's region
Only if the VM uses a managed disk
Only after moving the group's subscription
Resources in a group can be in different regions. The group location decides where its metadata is stored.
Which is the correct Azure management hierarchy, from top to bottom?
Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources
Subscriptions, management groups, resources, resource groups
Tenants, resource groups, subscriptions, resources
Resource groups, subscriptions, regions, resources
Management groups organize subscriptions, subscriptions contain resource groups, and resource groups contain resources. Policies and RBAC inherit downward.
You want to prevent anyone from deleting a production database while still allowing changes to it. What do you apply?
A CanNotDelete resource lock
A ReadOnly resource lock
A Contributor role assignment
A Deny rule in the database NSG
CanNotDelete allows reads and updates but blocks deletion. ReadOnly also blocks updates, which would break normal changes.
In Azure App Service, what does an App Service plan define?
The compute and pricing tier the apps run on
The source code repository for each app
The custom domain names of each app
The database connection strings of apps
Several web apps can share one plan and its VMs. Scaling the plan scales all apps in it.
How do you deploy a new version to App Service with near-zero downtime and an easy way back?
Deploy to a staging slot, then swap it with production
Stop the app, deploy the new build over it, then start it again
Create a brand new App Service plan for each release
Edit the files over FTP directly on the live app
Deployment slots let you warm up a release in staging and swap it into production. Swapping again restores the previous version.
In App Service, how do application settings reach a running app?
As environment variables
As a file named appsettings.azure
As command-line arguments
Only through Azure Key Vault calls
App settings are injected as environment variables. They can also reference Key Vault secrets.
Which command merges an AKS cluster's credentials into your local kubeconfig?
az aks get-credentials --resource-group RG --name NAME
az aks connect --resource-group RG --name NAME --merge-kubeconfig
kubectl login --aks --resource-group RG --name NAME
az login --kubernetes --resource-group RG --name NAME
az aks get-credentials writes the cluster context into ~/.kube/config so kubectl can use it.
AKS nodes fail to pull images from your Azure Container Registry with an authorization error. Which fix is simplest?
Attach the registry with az aks update --attach-acr
Make every Pod in the cluster run as privileged
Open port 443 in the AKS NSG to the ACR address only
Rebuild all the images from a public base image and push again
--attach-acr grants the cluster's kubelet identity the AcrPull role on the registry, so nodes can pull images.
In AKS, what is the purpose of a system node pool?
Hosting critical system Pods like CoreDNS
Running only GPU workloads for the cluster
Storing etcd data for the cluster control plane
Holding only the Windows nodes of the cluster
System pools run critical add-ons, and user pools run application workloads. The control plane is managed by Azure, not hosted in your pools.
An app appends log lines to a single file in Azure Storage. Which blob type fits this pattern?
Append blob
Block blob
Page blob
Archive blob
Append blobs are optimized for append-only writes like logs. Page blobs back random-access disks; Archive is a tier, not a blob type.
A blob in the Archive access tier must be read. What has to happen first?
It must be rehydrated to an online tier
It can be read directly but slowly
It must be copied to another account
It must be snapshotted first
Archive blobs are offline. You rehydrate them to an online tier such as Hot or Cool, which can take hours, before reading.
A partner needs to upload files into one container for 24 hours without an Azure account. What do you give them?
A SAS token scoped to the container
The storage account key
An Owner role on the subscription
A public anonymous container
A shared access signature grants limited, time-bound permissions. The account key gives full access to everything in the account.
How many IP addresses does Azure reserve in each virtual network subnet?
Azure reserves the network address, the broadcast address and three addresses for gateway and DNS, so a /24 offers 251 usable addresses.
VNet A is peered with B, and B is peered with C. Can VMs in A reach VMs in C through these peerings alone?
No, VNet peering is not transitive
Yes, peering is transitive by default
Yes, if all three are in one region
Only if C uses a public IP prefix
Peering connects exactly two VNets. To connect A and C, peer them directly or route through a hub with a gateway or firewall.
Two NSG rules match the same traffic: priority 100 denies it and priority 200 allows it. What happens?
It is denied, because lower numbers are processed first
It is allowed, because allow rules take precedence over deny rules
It is allowed, because higher priority numbers win
Both rules are merged, and the traffic is only logged
NSG rules are evaluated in priority order from the lowest number, and processing stops at the first match.
An Azure Functions timer trigger uses the schedule 0 */5 * * * *. How often does it run?
Every 5 minutes
Every 5 seconds
Every 5 hours
At 5 past each hour
Function timers use NCRONTAB with six fields, starting with seconds. Second 0 of every fifth minute means every 5 minutes.
You need a long-running, stateful workflow that chains several Azure Functions and waits for a human approval. Which extension fits?
Durable Functions
Function proxies
Application Insights
Azure Functions Core Tools
Durable Functions provides orchestrator functions that keep state across steps and can wait for external events.
What was Microsoft Entra ID called before its 2023 rename?
Azure Active Directory
Azure Identity Services
Microsoft Live Directory
Windows Server Active Directory
Microsoft renamed Azure AD to Microsoft Entra ID in 2023. Windows Server Active Directory is the separate on-premises directory service.
An App Service must read secrets from Key Vault without storing any credentials. Which Entra ID feature fits?
A managed identity for the app
An app password in app settings
A guest user invitation
A Conditional Access policy
A managed identity gives the app an Entra ID identity whose tokens Azure handles, so you grant it Key Vault access without secrets in config.
nebius-cloud: In a managed Kubernetes service such as Nebius Managed Kubernetes, what does the provider operate for you?
The control plane, including the API server and etcd
Your application Deployments, Services and their scaling
Your container images and the registries that hold them
Your Helm releases and the values they are deployed with
Managed Kubernetes means the provider runs and updates the control plane. You still define node groups and all workloads.
A training Pod on a managed Kubernetes GPU node group must get one GPU. What does its container spec need?
resources.limits with nvidia.com/gpu: 1
a nodeName set to the GPU node's name
an env var GPU=1 in the container spec
privileged: true together with hostNetwork
GPUs are exposed by the NVIDIA device plugin as the extended resource nvidia.com/gpu, which the scheduler counts like CPU or memory.
On a Kubernetes cluster with GPU nodes, which component typically installs drivers, the device plugin and GPU monitoring for you?
The NVIDIA GPU Operator
The Cluster Autoscaler
The CoreDNS add-on
The Ingress controller
The GPU Operator manages the NVIDIA software stack on nodes, including drivers, the container toolkit, the device plugin and DCGM metrics.
GPU nodes are tainted so regular Pods do not land on them. What must a GPU workload add to be scheduled there?
A matching toleration
A higher PriorityClass only
A hostPort mapping
A PodDisruptionBudget
Taints repel Pods that lack a matching toleration. Teams often add a nodeSelector or affinity as well so GPU Pods go only to GPU nodes.
A managed Kubernetes cluster should add GPU nodes only when training jobs are pending. What do you enable on the GPU node group?
Node autoscaling with a minimum of zero
A Horizontal Pod Autoscaler on CPU
A fixed node count of eight
A DaemonSet for each GPU job
The cluster autoscaler adds nodes when Pods cannot be scheduled and removes idle ones. A minimum of zero avoids paying for idle GPUs.
Why are multi-node GPU clusters for large model training connected with InfiniBand instead of only regular Ethernet?
It gives high bandwidth and low latency for collectives
It is required to install CUDA drivers on each of the nodes
It removes the need for large GPU memory per card
It encrypts all of the traffic between nodes
Distributed training syncs gradients across GPUs with collective operations. InfiniBand with RDMA keeps that communication from becoming the bottleneck.
Which NVIDIA library do PyTorch and similar frameworks use for fast all-reduce between GPUs across nodes?
NCCL
cuDNN
TensorRT
cuBLAS
NCCL implements collective communication over NVLink, PCIe and InfiniBand. cuDNN and cuBLAS are compute libraries, and TensorRT is for inference.
After creating a GPU virtual machine, which command quickly confirms that the driver sees the GPUs?
nvidia-smi
lspci --cuda
nvcc --gpus
docker info --gpu
nvidia-smi lists GPUs, driver and CUDA version, memory use and running processes. nvcc is the CUDA compiler and does not query devices.
Inside Docker on a GPU VM, a container cannot see the GPUs. With the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed, which flag fixes it?
--gpus all
--privileged-gpu
--device-gpu=1
--runtime=cuda
docker run --gpus all exposes the host GPUs through the NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
Nebius Object Storage is compatible with which API, which lets you use tools like the AWS CLI with a custom endpoint?
The Amazon S3 API
The Azure Blob REST API
The NFS v4 protocol
The HDFS API
Because it is S3-compatible, S3 SDKs and tools work after you set the provider's endpoint URL and credentials.
You use the AWS CLI against an S3-compatible bucket at another cloud provider. Which option points it at that provider?
--endpoint-url set to the provider's URL
--region set to the value global
--provider set to the cloud's name
--profile set to s3-compatible
The AWS CLI talks to AWS by default. --endpoint-url (or endpoint_url in the config) redirects requests to another S3-compatible service.
A training job saves large checkpoints that must survive node failures and be reused by later jobs. Where should they go?
Object storage or a shared network filesystem
The local boot disk of the training VM
A ConfigMap inside the Kubernetes cluster
GPU memory, kept warm between runs
Local disks disappear with the node, and ConfigMaps are limited to about 1 MiB. Durable shared storage keeps checkpoints available.
An object storage bucket holds a private dataset. What is the safest way to let one training service read it?
A service account with read-only access to that bucket
Making the bucket public for the length of the training run
Sharing your personal access keys with the training service
Giving the service admin rights on the whole project
Least privilege means a dedicated identity with only the read permission it needs, which can be revoked without affecting people.
Training code in CI must call the cloud API automatically. Which identity fits best?
A service account with only the roles it needs
The team lead's personal account and its credentials
A shared admin user used by all of the pipelines
An anonymous public endpoint with no authentication
Service accounts are meant for automation, and scoping their roles limits damage if credentials leak.
A GPU VM runs a Jupyter server. What is the safest way to reach it from your laptop?
An SSH tunnel, with the Jupyter port closed
Opening port 8888 to 0.0.0.0/0 for access
Disabling the Jupyter token for faster login
Giving the VM a second public IP for Jupyter
Port forwarding over SSH keeps the notebook off the public internet. Exposing an open Jupyter port lets anyone run code on your GPU machine.
A team wants to stop people from storing cloud access keys in a Git repository. Which practice helps most?
Store keys in a secrets manager, inject at runtime
Commit the keys, but only to a private Git repository
Encode the keys in base64 inside the source code
Rotate the keys once a year and keep them in Git
Secrets managers or CI secret stores keep keys out of history. Base64 is not encryption, and private repos still leak.
When you create a Linux compute instance on a cloud like Nebius, how do you usually get SSH access to it?
Pass your public SSH key at creation, via cloud-init
Upload your private SSH key to the new VM after creation
Use the default root password listed in the provider docs
Open port 22 and log in as root with a password
The cloud injects your public key into the instance. The private key never leaves your machine.
Your PyTorch training script will run on a fresh GPU VM. What saves the most setup time?
A boot image with GPU drivers and CUDA preinstalled
A generic minimal OS image that you configure yourself
Installing GPU drivers inside every container at start
Compiling the Linux kernel on the first boot of the VM
GPU cloud providers offer images with drivers and CUDA ready, so the VM can run GPU workloads right after boot.
A VM's boot disk is deleted when the VM is deleted, but you need a dataset to outlive it. What do you attach?
A separate data disk kept on VM deletion
More vCPUs added to the same instance
A larger swap file on the boot disk
A second network interface on the VM
A separate data disk has its own lifecycle and can be detached and attached to a new VM later.
An 8-GPU instance sits idle overnight between experiments. What is the simplest way to cut its cost without losing its disk?
Stop it, and start it again when needed
Lower its vCPU count while it keeps running
Delete its boot disk but keep the VM
Move it into a different project overnight
On most clouds a stopped VM is not billed for compute, while its disks are kept (and billed as storage).
cloudflare: A DNS record in Cloudflare shows the orange cloud (Proxied). What does that mean?
Traffic passes through Cloudflare, hiding the origin IP
Cloudflare only answers DNS queries for the record, nothing else
The record stays disabled until it is verified
Email sent to the domain is filtered for spam
Proxied records resolve to Cloudflare IPs, so Cloudflare can cache, protect and terminate TLS. DNS only (grey cloud) returns the origin IP.
Which DNS record type cannot be proxied through Cloudflare?
MX
A
AAAA
CNAME
Only A, AAAA and CNAME records that serve HTTP traffic can be proxied. MX and TXT records are always DNS only.
You want the root domain example.com to point at a hostname such as myapp.example.net. Which Cloudflare feature makes this possible?
CNAME flattening
DNSSEC signing
Argo Smart Routing
Load Balancing pools
A CNAME at the apex conflicts with standard DNS rules. Cloudflare flattens it by answering with the target's IP addresses instead.
Which record type would you add to prove domain ownership to a third-party service or to publish SPF?
TXT
MX
SRV
PTR
TXT records hold arbitrary text such as verification tokens and SPF policies.
With default settings, which response does Cloudflare's CDN cache?
Static files like .css, .js and images
Every HTML page on the whole site
All JSON responses from your API
Responses to POST form submissions
By default Cloudflare caches based on file extension for static assets. HTML is not cached unless a rule tells it to.
A response header shows cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC. What does it mean?
The asset was not eligible for caching
The asset was served from the cache
The cache entry for it had expired
The origin server was down at the time
DYNAMIC means Cloudflare did not consider the asset cacheable, for example HTML under default settings. HIT means served from cache.
You deployed new CSS, but visitors still get the old file from Cloudflare. What fixes it right away?
Purge the cached file or the whole cache
Switch the DNS record to DNS only for a whole day
Enable DNSSEC signing on the whole zone
Lower the DNS TTL to 60 seconds
Purging removes cached copies so the next request fetches the new file. Versioned file names avoid this in the future.
Your origin sends Cache-Control: private for a user dashboard. What does Cloudflare do with it?
It does not cache the response
It caches it for one hour
It caches it per visitor IP
It caches it but hides it from search
private tells shared caches like CDNs not to store the response. Only the user's browser may cache it.
Where does Cloudflare Workers code run?
On Cloudflare's edge network in V8 isolates
In a container that runs on your own origin server
In the visitor's browser tab, as a service worker
On one central VM that is created per account
Workers run close to users across Cloudflare's data centers. V8 isolates start much faster than containers.
Which module Worker skeleton handles incoming HTTP requests?
export default { async fetch(request, env, ctx) { } }
export default { async handle(req, res) { } }
module.exports = (req, res) => { }
export function main(event, context) { }
Module Workers export an object with a fetch handler that returns a Response. env holds bindings, and ctx exposes waitUntil.
Which command-line tool is used to develop and deploy Cloudflare Workers?
wrangler
cfctl
workerd-cli
flarectl deploy
wrangler runs local dev with wrangler dev and publishes with wrangler deploy.
A Worker returns a response but must also send analytics to another API without delaying the user. Which call fits?
ctx.waitUntil(sendAnalytics())
await sendAnalytics() before returning
setTimeout(sendAnalytics, 0)
process.nextTick(sendAnalytics)
waitUntil keeps the Worker alive for background work after the response is sent. Awaiting first delays the response.
Your Worker needs a counter that is strongly consistent across all users worldwide. Which product fits better than Workers KV?
Durable Objects
Workers Sites
The Cache API
KV with a short TTL
KV is eventually consistent and optimized for reads. Durable Objects give a single, strongly consistent place for state.
Attackers hit your site through Cloudflare, then switch to attacking the origin IP directly. What is the best fix on the origin?
Accept web traffic only from Cloudflare IPs
Enable Under Attack Mode on the zone
Lower the DNS TTL of the origin A record to one minute
Add more Page Rules for the domain
Cloudflare only protects traffic that passes through it. Locking the origin firewall to Cloudflare's ranges (or using Cloudflare Tunnel) blocks direct attacks.
What does Cloudflare's I'm Under Attack mode do for visitors?
Shows a browser check page before the site
Blocks every visitor outside your country
Turns off caching for the entire zone
Redirects all traffic to a status page
It adds a JavaScript challenge to filter out bots during a layer 7 attack, at the cost of a short delay for real visitors.
SSL/TLS mode is Flexible, and the origin redirects HTTP to HTTPS. What do visitors see?
A redirect loop (too many redirects)
A valid page served normally over HTTPS
A certificate name mismatch error in the browser
A 521 error saying the origin is down
Flexible connects to the origin over plain HTTP. The origin redirects to HTTPS, Cloudflare requests HTTP again, and the loop repeats. Full or Full (strict) fixes it.
What is the difference between Full and Full (strict) SSL/TLS modes?
Strict also validates the origin certificate
Strict uses HTTP/3 for connections to the origin
Full encrypts only the visitor side of the traffic
Strict disables TLS 1.2 for all visitors
Both encrypt Cloudflare-to-origin traffic. Full accepts any certificate, including self-signed; Full (strict) requires a valid, trusted one such as a Cloudflare Origin CA cert.
Two Page Rules match the same URL. How does Cloudflare apply them?
Only the highest-priority match is applied
All of the matching rules are merged
The most recently created rule wins
The rule with the most settings wins
Page Rules are evaluated in priority order and only the first match takes effect. Newer Rules products such as Cache Rules and Redirect Rules are replacing them.
A Page Rule forwards example.com/blog/* to https://blog.example.com/$1. Where does example.com/blog/post-1 go?
https://blog.example.com/post-1
https://blog.example.com/blog/post-1
https://blog.example.com/$1
https://blog.example.com/
$1 is replaced with the text matched by the first * wildcard, which here is post-1.
Bots hammer your /login endpoint. Which Cloudflare WAF feature directly limits requests per IP to that path?
A rate limiting rule matching the /login path
A managed OWASP ruleset running in log-only mode on /login
A DNS-only record for the login subdomain
Browser Cache TTL set to one year for /login
Rate limiting rules count requests matching an expression, such as http.request.uri.path eq "/login", and block or challenge clients above the threshold.
vercel: In a Vercel project without a framework, where do you put files so each becomes a serverless function?
In the api/ directory at the root
In a functions/ directory at the root
In public/api/ next to static files
In a vercel/functions/ directory
Files such as api/hello.js become endpoints like /api/hello. Frameworks like Next.js use their own conventions.
A Vercel serverless function writes uploaded files to a local folder and expects them on the next request. What goes wrong?
The local filesystem does not persist between calls
Vercel blocks every write to the disk at runtime, even to /tmp
Files are copied to all regions instantly
The function is converted into an edge function
Functions are stateless, and only temporary scratch space like /tmp is writable. Persistent data belongs in a database or object storage.
Which signature is the classic Node.js handler for api/hello.js on Vercel?
export default function handler(req, res) { }
exports.main = (event, context) => { }
export async function onRequest(context) { }
addEventListener('fetch', (event) => handler(event))
The Node.js runtime passes request and response objects similar to Express. The other forms belong to AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Pages and service workers.
In a Next.js 15 project on Vercel, where does Middleware live?
In a middleware file at the project root or in src
In pages/_middleware.js inside each route folder
In vercel.json under a middleware key
In api/middleware.js next to the functions
Next.js expects middleware.ts (or .js) at the root or in src, and its matcher config limits which paths it runs on. Next.js 16 renamed this file to proxy.
When does Vercel Middleware run relative to the cache?
Before the cache, on each matched request
After the response has been stored in the cache
Only when the cache lookup results in a miss
Only once, during the build step of the project
Middleware runs before routing and caching, so it suits redirects, auth checks and rewrites, but slow code delays every request.
Middleware should show /maintenance content while the browser URL stays the same. Which call fits?
NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/maintenance', req.url))
NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/maintenance', req.url))
NextResponse.next({ path: '/maintenance' })
Response.json({ path: '/maintenance' })
rewrite serves another path's content under the original URL. redirect sends the browser to the new URL, changing the address bar.
Code using fs.readFileSync fails when moved to the Edge runtime. Why?
The Edge runtime lacks Node.js APIs like fs
The Edge runtime only supports Python code, not JS
Using fs requires a paid Vercel plan
The file must be base64-encoded first
The Edge runtime is built on Web APIs like fetch and Request. Node-only modules such as fs are not available.
You push a commit to branch feature/login in a repository connected to Vercel. What happens by default?
A preview deployment with its own URL
Production is updated immediately
Nothing until you run vercel --prod
The branch is merged into main for you
Every push to a non-production branch gets a preview deployment, and pull requests show its link.
Which pushes trigger a production deployment in a default Git-connected Vercel project?
Pushes to the production branch, usually main
Pushes to any branch with a tag
Only manual deploys from the dashboard
Pushes to a branch that is named production only
The production branch is set in project settings and defaults to the repository's main branch.
An API key should be available in preview deployments but differ from the production key. How do you set it up?
Add it twice, scoped to Preview and Production
Commit two separate .env files to the Git repository
Use one variable and check the URL in code
Store both values in vercel.json under env
Vercel environment variables are scoped to Production, Preview and Development, and can even target specific preview branches.
You changed an environment variable in the Vercel dashboard, but the live site still uses the old value. Why?
Variable changes apply only to new deployments
The variable needs a VERCEL_ prefix to be read
Variables are only updated at midnight UTC each day
The browser cached the old variable value locally
Values are captured at build and deploy time. Redeploy to pick up the change.
A Vite app on Vercel reads import.meta.env.API_URL in the browser, but it is undefined. What fixes it?
Rename the variable to VITE_API_URL
Mark the variable as sensitive
Move it to the Development scope
Read it with process.env.API_URL
Vite only exposes variables prefixed with VITE_ to client code. Never put secrets in such variables, since they ship to the browser.
Which Vercel CLI command downloads the Development environment variables into a local file?
vercel env pull .env.local
vercel env export .env.local
vercel secrets get --all
vercel dev --sync-env
vercel env pull writes the project's variables for the chosen environment, Development by default, to a local env file.
A build fails because of a corrupted dependency cache. Which CLI option deploys while skipping the build cache?
vercel --force
vercel --clean
vercel --no-cache-ever
vercel --fresh-install
vercel --force creates a new deployment without the build cache. The dashboard offers the same option when you redeploy.
Why do repeat builds on Vercel usually finish faster than the first one?
Dependencies and framework caches are reused
Later builds always use larger machines
Later builds run on the client's machine
The second build reuses the old output as-is
Vercel restores cached installs and framework build caches, such as Next.js's .next/cache, between deployments.
In a Turborepo monorepo on Vercel, what lets unchanged packages skip rebuilding across deployments?
Remote Caching of task outputs
Preview deployment protection
Edge Config storage
A larger function memory size
Turborepo hashes task inputs and reuses cached outputs from Vercel Remote Cache when nothing changed.
You add www.example.com to a Vercel project but keep your current DNS provider. Which record do you usually create?
A CNAME record to the target Vercel shows
An MX record pointing to Vercel servers
A TXT record containing your project name
An NS record delegating the www label
Subdomains are usually connected with a CNAME to the value in the Vercel domain settings. Apex domains use an A record or Vercel nameservers.
After you add and verify a domain in Vercel, how is the HTTPS certificate handled?
Vercel issues and renews it automatically
You must upload a certificate yearly
HTTPS needs a separate CDN in front
It works only on vercel.app subdomains
Vercel provisions and renews TLS certificates for verified domains automatically.
Your single-page app on Vercel returns 404 when users refresh a client-side route like /profile. Which vercel.json setting fixes it?
A rewrite from /(.*) to /index.html
A redirect from /(.*) to / on every path
A header rule adding Cache-Control
A cleanUrls setting set to false
The rewrite serves index.html for unknown paths while keeping the URL, so the client router can render the route. A redirect would lose the path.
A bad release is live in production. What is the fastest way on Vercel to restore the previous version without rebuilding?
Instant Rollback to an earlier production build
Revert the commit and wait for a new build
Delete the project and deploy it again
Rename the production branch in settings
Instant Rollback points production domains back to an earlier deployment that is already built, so it takes effect quickly.
